chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who wakes up in the morning intending to fast, then it occurs to him to break it, so he breaks it. He said: 'He has the choice between himself and midday.' I said: 'Does he make it up if he breaks it?' He said: 'Yes, because it is a good deed which he intended to perform, so let him complete it.' I said: 'If a man intends to fast from the rising of the day, does he fast?' He said: 'Yes.'

key_terms.يُبْدِي لَهُ: It occurs to him / He decides

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who intends to fast in the morning but breaks it before midday?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the voluntary nature of the morning intention allows for flexibility, permitting the individual to break the fast before midday without invalidating the reward of their initial intent. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that good intentions in voluntary acts carry merit even if the action is not completed, distinguishing it from obligatory acts where completion is strictly required.
